steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: (Yawns)

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Ooo! New senbei flavors! 'Premium muskmelon with Siracusan red sauce' and 'condensed cystymilk with honjouzou soy sauce'...

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: They look delicious.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: No. I'm counting my calories! I have to watch what I eat!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Huh? Mio-san?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I'll be at the agency in just a few minutes. Did you need something?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Almost there. I'm running over now!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: 'Treating fans like fools, nose in the air'...

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: 'I'm no fan of hers anymore, that's for sure. She ruined the concert!'...

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: 'Trying so hard to go viral, pretending to be scared—aren't you embarrassed?'...

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: What... what is all this?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: A media smear campaign. It started early yesterday morning—most likely the work of a rival.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Producer.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Producer! I didn't know you were coming!

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: What's the situation?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: It all happened so suddenly. PR is still investigating.

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: This isn't just PR.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: That 'one-horned Oni' wasn't our doing, right?

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Mio, you are responsible for Momoka's safety. Please get to the bottom of all this.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Momoka, your gaffe on stage yesterday was one thing, but upstairs is more upset about something else.

spans.text: Momoka, your gaffe on stage yesterday was one thing, but
is more upset about something else.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: What's that...?

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: You've been acting less and less like a pop idol lately. Then this happens, and you vanish without a trace?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: The fans didn't seem to react too negatively. I even gave them an encore. They were into it.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I was tired and hungry when I hopped offstage, not to mention scared. I just went to my favorite oden yatai, is all.

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Well, how do you explain your inappropriate monologue up there?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: 'Inappropriate monologue'?! What, what did I say wrong?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Your remarks on Kajimachi.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Kajimachi? Oh. You mean the fan that——

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: The Kinseki Group is the sole backer of our entire operation. They have a very tense relationship with Kajimachi right now—speaking out recklessly will only make things harder for all of us.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I don't understand what the big deal is. I was just thinking about how I shot my first movie there.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I still remember when I got started. You told me Chairman Tessai valued my skills...

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: The past is the past. I'm talking about the present. Things are different now.

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Besides, we've always told you to stay in your lane and stick to the script when you're onstage. The people come to see Momoka, not you, with your big mouth.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I... I get it.

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: As long as you get it.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Producer, when are we going to the recording studio? My schedule is packed today. We have to get a move on.

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Meh. Actually, why don't you take a few days off.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: HUH? What?!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: P-Producer! I don't need any rest! I'm used to the grind by now! We're in peak season. I know that. If I take a break now, that put us several days behind!

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Maybe if you hadn't been so busy during the day yesterday, you would have been calmer last night.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I'm sorry, but——

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: If you really want to make up for your mistakes, Momoka, I have an urgent assignment for you.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Anything!

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: The television station wants to book you on a show. Take a look.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: The Haunted House of Kajimachi?! Another one of these shows? Why?!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: And why now, of all times, would they produce a program that makes Kajimachi look bad?

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Then you'd rather take a break?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: No! I just...

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Momoka, you know that when you don't do what we say... it reflects... poorly on you.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Momoka!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Producer, I don't want to die!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I've known that place was haunted for forever! A bunch of people died in that house!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: They say it's... it's somehow connected to the 'Nameless Oni'. It was her there on the stage last night...

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: Momoka, I will take measures to ensure your safety.

steps.name: Producer
steps.text: (Quietly) Mio, back me up here.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Momoka, do not worry. I'll go with you.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Mio-san... is going too?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Are you strong enough to take down that vicious Oni?
Mio tilts her head and thinks hard for a few seconds.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Maybe not.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I'm doomed. I'm done for!

a.text: 'If we keep walking down Nita Street, we'll soon arrive at Kajimachi. From now on, that will be our place, our city.'
'Our city? But, Papa, we've been walking down the street, and I don't see anything all that different. What do you think, Uncle Tessai?'
'It will become different. It will change.'

steps.text: A wind carrying a scent—woody, or perhaps musty—blows against her face, and somehow, Hoshiguma is compelled to take a deep breath.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: The houses are all so old.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Does Uncle Tessai still live in the same place?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Yeah. The big house at the end there.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Kinbee, what's the deal with the funeral? Kajimachi looks like it's doing fine?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: It's a long story.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: What's wrong?
Hoshiguma quickly realizes why Kinbee has fallen silent—and why the expression on his face now carries a touch more respect.
Not too far away, there's an old man standing in the road, facing them.
The old man's back is slightly hunched. Yet somehow, as the wind lifts his wide sleeves, he seems to stand a little taller.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Uncle Tessai!

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Chairman Tessai.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Kinbee, I told you that you are not permitted to set foot in Kajimachi ever again.
The Phidia appears startled. The reverence on his face quickly turns to fear.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: I was preoccupied with a certain 'happy event' that happened today. I lost track of my surroundings and accidentally walked into Kajimachi. Damn!

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: She's in cahoots with you. That's what you're happy about?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Chairman, I just got her out of the police station, is all. The cops started chasing her as soon as she arrived in Mitsukue. She only just slipped out.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: She's come back here out of genuine concern for her home. If you're unhappy about something, please, take it up with me. Do not blame her!

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: As for my trespassing into Kajimachi—shall I'll perform a dogeza, offer a formal apology on another date, or cut off a finger—

spans.text: As for my trespassing into Kajimachi—shall I'll perform a
, offer a formal apology on another date, or cut off a finger—

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Ha! You'd do any of those things if I asked?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: The decision is yours—

steps.name: Reckless Yakuza
steps.text: *huff huff* Oyabun! I ran around to everyone asking where you were, until I found out you'd come here to Kajimachi!

steps.name: Reckless Yakuza
steps.text: Why did you make the trip out here? That old bastard doesn't have many days left—why bother coming to this forsaken place?

steps.name: Reckless Yakuza
steps.text: O-Oyabun?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: You know I'm your oyabun?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Then do you know who gave this 'oyabun' the lofty position that he holds today?

steps.name: Reckless Yakuza
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Ah, right, this isn't your first offense.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Some time ago, Chairman Tessai forbade me and my men from ever entering Kajimachi again. This is not the first time you've disobeyed that order. Am I right?

steps.name: Reckless Yakuza
steps.text: Well, I wasn't—

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: You were the one who drove those three families out of Kajimachi—plus the two shops that had to shut down, and that was all after Chairman Tessai ordered us to stay out of Kajimachi. Isn't that right?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: You knowingly went against his orders. How should we punish you?
Beads of sweat form on the flustered gangster's forehead.
The oyabun isn't usually like this—he toasts me when I do well and offers gentle encouragement when I fall short.
Before he can even finish his thought, he hears a sound.
*swish*

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Kinbee, what are you doing?!
Before he can even finish his thought, it's cut short—the gangster's headless body collapses to the ground with a thud.
Neither Tessai's iron fan nor Hoshiguma's Hannya can match the quick draw of the Phidia's long sword.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: That was your Kinsekikai brother!

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Murdering a member of the family right in front of me. Is this your way of raising a hand against me?

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: But Chairman, you've already given me managerial control of the clan.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: He ignored warnings, defied the chairman, and refused to change—he should've died long ago. The fact that he lived this long is a failure of my leadership.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Well, I brought her here; my work is done. It's time I answered for disobeying Chairman Tessai's orders.
He aims his bloodstained long sword—still unsheathed—at his finger.
Before the old man can even speak, the Phidia swings his blade, and his left pinkie falls to the floor.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: There. That should atone for my sins, yeah?
No one says anything.
The Phidia slides the blade back into its sheath, bows deeply to Tessai, and gives a small nod to Hoshiguma.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Chairman Tessai, I will now take my leave, so as not to bother you further.

steps.name: Mifune
steps.text: Welcome home, Hoshiguma.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I'm going to call the police—
Hoshiguma's voice trails off, as she becomes lost in thought, remembering how Kinbee swaggered around the police station.
The old man squints his eyes slightly, as he glances at Hoshiguma.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: It seems you've been getting on well in Lungmen. You've forsaken the life of crime, eh?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: If you still walked the path, you would remember this—no matter how a man dies, someone always comes to clean up.

spans.text: If you still walked the path, you would remember this—no matter how a man dies, someone always comes to

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: And as long as the cleanup happens, the police won't bother themselves with our 'messes'.

spans.text: happens, the police won't bother themselves with our 'messes'.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: You've had a long trip. Let's talk inside.
Though she has been away for twenty years, Hoshiguma still pushes open the gate with practiced ease.
Just like in Kajimachi, time has not left much of a mark on this place. Hoshiguma immediately spots the little path she used to take—the quickest way across the courtyard.
She can't tell whether the koi in the pond have lived all these years, or if the owner has been quietly replacing them with identical ones.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I'm back.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Sit.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Uncle Tessai, did you write me that letter because Kinbee—

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: I never wrote you a letter.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: It wasn't you?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: When you left Mitsukue twenty years ago, I told you we would never again make contact. I intended to honor that promise.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: So, that letter...?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Kinbee forged it. What else could it be?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Why would he do that? You're the chairman of the Kinsekikai. How could you permit such a transgression?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Chairman? If that viper didn't keep calling me that, I'd have forgotten I was chairman of anything.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Look, I'm an old man with no real power. Even my last parcel of turf, Kajimachi, is about to be taken from me.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: And Kinbee... heh, he's taken over the Originium crystal business that I built from the ground up. He's taken control of all our operations.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: He's started new ventures like a TV network and even a talent agency, and made them hugely successful.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: So he's usurped all Kinsekikai businesses and is now planning to take over Kajimachi?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: 'A radical rebirth and redevelopment plan' — that was how he put it, just a month ago.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Who's rebirthing what? How are they redeveloping it? Who keeps the proceeds? Ha. These are not questions I can ask, of course.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: That's why you forbade him and his men from entering Kajimachi.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: And today we get this grand performance, where he uses his minion's life as a stage prop… no, not a performance, it was a show of force.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: He didn't use to be like this.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: He was a better actor back then. He tricked me, and he tricked you. That's the only possible explanation, no?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: You didn't realize that finger-chopping bit was all a ploy?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: A... a ploy?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: A fake finger? Surgical reattachment? A prosthesis? He's got no shortage of tricks.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: He wasn't 'atoning for his sins'. He was spitting in my face! He was making a mockery of the Kinsekikai, of everything we stand for.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: I don't know what scheme Kinbee had in bringing you back, but there's only one thing you should do now: return to Lungmen, and don't ever come back again. He's a rabid tuskbeast now.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: But what will happen to you?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Me? As long as the Kinsekikai still exist, I'm still their chairman by title. Kinbee wouldn't dare raise a hand against me, at least not out in the open. And that's enough.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I can't just leave.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Then what do you intend to do? Wait until Kinbee has pushed me to the brink and then end my suffering?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I just don't want any more regrets this time.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: So you regret going to Lungmen?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: No. Everything I regret... is from my time in Mitsukue.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Watching Kinbee cut that man's head off like it was nothing... it sent all kinds of regret bubbling up from my stomach.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Kinbee's men see Kajimachi as nothing more than a pimple on Mitsukue's hide. You can't change their minds about that.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I'm going to do whatever I can.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: By the way, amidst our grim conversation I almost forgot to ask... what happened with Hannya? When Kinbee was here, I took a glance at it. Looks different than it did the day I gave it to you, no?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Well, to be honest, a corner got sliced off.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: How?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: With a sword.
The old man's world-weary gaze suddenly flares with intensity.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Whose sword? What was it made of? How was their sword technique? Did they use any Arts?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: A good friend of mine back in Lungmen, a colleague—

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Explaining it all with words is going to take too long. Give Hannya to me. Let me see it.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Huh—tsk tsk...

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: A cut like this doesn't come from advanced reinforced steel or simple Arts alone. Sure, there's always someone stronger out there—but let's not forget, Hannya's no ordinary shield.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: ...Chi Xiao.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Uncle Tessai, you can tell just by looking at the cut?!

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Don't forget, I've been around. Back when I was knocking back drinks with the Yanese trade envoys, the name 'Chi Xiao' came up more than once.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: For Hannya, being bested by Chi Xiao is no shame at all.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: At the end of the day, it wasn't sharpness or toughness that turned Chi Xiao and Hannya into legendary weapons.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Your mind was weaker than Chi Xiao's wielder. Not by much, but enough to turn the tide of battle.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: In that case, I guess Kinbee's letter wasn't totally useless. At least it gave Hannya a chance.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Do you want to reforge it?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Of course. Do you expect me to let you run around Lungmen with this broken shield?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Still... I need to think for a bit about how I'll reforge this shield, to give you a sliver of a chance to best Chi Xiao. Let me think it over...
The old man, who once stared down disaster unblinking, now burns with the impatience of youth. He's learned that there's someone stronger out there, and he yearns to test his mettle.
The old acquaintance's long sword has just shattered any sort of 'parting sorrow', yet nostalgia stirs in Hoshiguma all the same.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: Heh. Forget it. This isn't something you and I can figure out by just sitting here and thinking about it. Give me some time.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: You've spent all night in an interrogation room. You must be tired. Go to the guest room and get some sleep.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I want to pay my respects to my father first.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: He's your biological father. What are you apologizing to me for?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Is that clinic, my old home, still there?

steps.name: Tessai
steps.text: It's there, but no one has lived in it for about a decade. I'd bet it doesn't much resemble its former self.
The abandoned house in the alley at the end of Kajimachi's North Street... everyone calls it the 'Haunted House'.
After the vicious Oni disappeared, Shimasu, who was the shateigashira, moved into the house with his family, but within three months, he fell ill and passed away.
Six months later, Sanoguchi, who was then serving as wakagashira-hosa, bought the house. After hiring an onmyoji to perform rites for seven days and nights, he moved in with his new bride.

On the seventh night, a patrolman heard wretched wails coming from the 'Haunted House'. In a fit of madness, Sanoguchi took up his family's heirloom blade, killed his wife, and then took his own life.
In the years that followed, every soul who deigned to live in the Haunted House met a terrible end. Eventually, no one dared go near it again.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Legend has it that the vicious Oni never really disappeared. From time to time, her tortured visage will pop up in the Haunted House.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: And so, today...

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: It's too dark in here. I can't see anything...

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: (Lights lantern) M-Mio-san, are you there?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Whoa!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: It's a pull-top!

steps.name: Voice in Earphones
steps.text: Momoka, calm down. The camera on your head is shaking all over the place.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Where did Mio-san go? She said she'd be here with me.

steps.name: Voice in Earphones
steps.text: She's feeling under the weather. She called in sick today.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I've known Mio-san for years, and I've never seen her get sick. Last winter, I watched her eat twenty ice creams with my own eyes, and she was completely fine. You're telling me she caught a cold? I don't believe it.

steps.name: Voice in Earphones
steps.text: Momoka, we're just trying to add some color here for TV. Work with us, okay?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: But I just saw that Oni at the stage, and now I'm going to visit her haunted house...

steps.name: Voice in Earphones
steps.text: Ugh. Relax. You're going to be fine.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Alright... I'll do my best.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Ugh, why are there so many pull-tops here?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I don't like this... Wait! What's that sound behind me?
Who's there?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: The vicious Oni? A ghost?!
It's you? What are you doing in my house?
Momoka grabs something shaped like a stick from the ground and points it at the shadowy figure.
But she quickly realizes that whatever she has picked up will be ineffective against ghosts or a fierce, vicious Oni. In a hurry, she shoves the stick-thing into her coat and pulls out a box...
...of roasted soybeans.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Vicious Oni! I-I've got roasted soybeans! If you dare come closer, I'll waste you!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Oni wa soto! Fuku wa uchi! Oni wa soto, fuku... fuku... err... uh...

spans.text: Oni wa soto! Fuku wa uchi! Oni wa soto, fuku... fuku... err... uh...

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: The beans aren't working. But I have some salt here too! Check it out! Salt!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: The thing... you... fear... most...

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: Well, I guess I'll be going. Sorry for intruding. Sorry for bothering you. Byebye. Sayounara!

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Hey! Wait a second!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: No, I don't think I will!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: My head!

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Are you alright?
Momoka, who has just struck her head on something, starts to fall to the ground. However, 'the ghost's' voice jolts her back on her feet.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I'm fine. I'm fine. Sorry for bothering you.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: I've got uh, kids, and my parents, they're so old... to take care of back home!

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: No! Hasuke is at home, waiting for me to water him! Let me go! I have to go take care of him!
In her panic, Momoka lets out a high note she's never even hit in the recording studio.
Later that day, as the production team looks at the footage, they are unsure which one of the two, Momoka or Hoshiguma, most resembles a wailing wraith.

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: What... what is that thing at my feet?!

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: You're asking me?

steps.name: Momoka
steps.text: No! I didn't ask you! Let me go!
The terrified girl suddenly disappears, kicking up a massive cloud of dust.
Perplexed, Hoshiguma leans in for a closer look, and finally sees what happened.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: She smashed right through the floorboards.
